about.beta: This is a beta. Keep the restore point option ticked when applying, and tell us in Issues if something doesn't work.
about.what: PitCrew is a free, open-source program that makes Windows 10 and 11 faster, cleaner and more private, without hidden risks. The name comes from the racing pit crew: in a few seconds they change the tires and tune the car without taking it out of the race.
about.features:
Performance, privacy and Explorer: {0} settings, each with the source that backs it up.
Startup: choose what opens with Windows, with the same switch Task Manager uses.
Cleanup: temporary files, the Recycle Bin, Windows Update leftovers and error reports.
Memory: how much is in use and which programs use the most, with a polite way to close them.
Maintenance: system repair (SFC and DISM), drive optimization and error check, disk health and a backup of every driver.
Built-in apps: removes the ones you don't use, with a way to reinstall them from the Microsoft Store.
Drivers: looks for updates in Windows Update and points out which ones are worth installing.
Restore points and history: everything PitCrew changed can be undone.
about.goal: To give anyone the care a good technician would give their PC, with three rules: only settings with a real, documented effect; nothing is applied before you see it; and everything can be put back exactly as it was. Popular tweaks that don't meet these rules are left out, with the reason, in docs/NOT-INCLUDED.md.
about.authorBio: I'm a data engineer. Before working with data, I spent years in IT support and IT coordination, where I led the information security committee through the ISO 27001 and ISO 27701 certifications. In my spare time I make Android games and open tools like this one. PitCrew started as a small script to update my PC's drivers and grew from there.

page.maintenance.title: Maintenance
page.maintenance.intro: Repairs and checks that Windows can run on its own but hides away. Pick what to run.
page.restore.title: Restore points
page.restore.intro: A restore point is a snapshot of Windows settings, drivers and programs. If something goes wrong, System Restore takes the PC back to it. Your documents are not affected.

maintenance.repair: Check and repair Windows system files
maintenance.repair.detail: Runs DISM (RestoreHealth) and then SFC. Fixes damaged Windows files that cause crashes and odd errors. Takes 10 to 40 minutes and downloads repair files from Windows Update if needed.
maintenance.componentCleanup.detail: DISM StartComponentCleanup: deletes superseded versions of updated system files. Updates installed so far can still be uninstalled.
maintenance.diskHealth.detail: Reads what each drive reports about itself (health, wear, temperature, errors). Changes nothing.
maintenance.driverBackup.detail: Copies every driver not included with Windows to a folder in Documents. Handy before reinstalling Windows. Can take more than 1 GB with graphics drivers.
maintenance.confirmLong: "{0}" can take 10 to 40 minutes, and PitCrew stays busy until it finishes. Continue?

page.memory.title: Memory
page.memory.intro: How much memory is in use and which programs use the most. Closing a program here works like clicking its X: it can ask you to save first.
memory.note: PitCrew doesn't "clean" memory: Windows already uses free memory as a cache and hands it to whichever program needs it. Emptying it by force makes programs reload from disk, which is slower (see docs/NOT-INCLUDED.md). If memory is always full, close what you don't use below, check Startup apps, or consider more RAM.

page.devices.title: Device power
page.devices.intro: Windows can turn some devices off to save power. If the Wi-Fi or the network drops, or the mouse, the keyboard or a USB device stops responding after a while, keep just that one always on. This is the "Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power" box in Device Manager, for every device in one place.

devices.infoDesktop: On a desktop, keeping a device always on costs almost nothing. Change only what gives you trouble; every change can be undone here or in History. For the internet, a network cable is steadier than Wi-Fi.
devices.infoLaptop: This is a laptop: a device kept always on uses more battery, and Microsoft advises against it on PCs with Modern Standby. Change only the device that gives you trouble; every change can be undone here or in History.

dashboard.analysisText: Not sure where to start? Pick a profile and PitCrew recommends what to tweak, clean and remove. You review everything before applying.
page.analysis.title: Automatic analysis
page.analysis.intro: Pick one or more profiles and PitCrew checks the PC: what can be tweaked, cleaned, removed and taken out of startup. You review the list, untick what you don't want and apply it all at once.
analysis.notice: This analysis is automatic. The recommendations come from a fixed, reviewed list and don't know how you use your PC. Check each item before applying: the choice, and the responsibility, are yours. Tweaks can be undone in History; cleanup can't be undone; removed apps can be reinstalled in Built-in apps, with internet (a restore point doesn't bring apps back); programs taken out of startup can be turned back on in Startup apps.
